Gujarat put on red alert for extremely heavy rain; flash flood warning issued by IMD
IMD has issued a red alert for Friday for Narmada, Ahmedabad, Anand, Vadodara, Chhota Udepur, Bharuch, Surat, Tapi, Dang, Navsari, Valsad, Daman, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Bhavnagar and Botad, warning of exceptionally heavy rainfall in these districts.
Gujarat is bracing for another spell of extremely heavy rainfall on Friday and Saturday, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing a red alert as a deep depression tracks westward across central India towards the state. The system, reinforced by a shear zone, an offshore trough and an active Western Disturbance, is expected to keep rainfall intense across several districts before easing from Sunday.
The fresh warning follows a week of extreme weather in Gujarat, with flood-like conditions in parts of South Gujarat and severe waterlogging in Ahmedabad.
According to IMD, the deep depression is currently centred over west-central Chhattisgarh, Vidarbha and southeast Madhya Pradesh, moving west-southwest at roughly 15 kmph. It is expected to weaken into a depression within 24 hours, though its path across southern Madhya Pradesh is likely to carry it towards Gujarat.
IMD said the combined effect of the depression, the offshore trough, the shear zone and the Western Disturbance is expected to produce widespread rainfall across the state through Friday and Saturday.
IMD has issued a red alert for Friday for Narmada, Ahmedabad, Anand, Vadodara, Chhota Udepur, Bharuch, Surat, Tapi, Dang, Navsari, Valsad, Daman, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Bhavnagar and Botad, warning of exceptionally heavy rainfall in these districts.
Vadodara is forecast to see temperatures between 26 and 31 degrees Celsius, along with thunderstorms, rain and extremely heavy rainfall.
An orange alert has also been issued by IMD for Gandhinagar, Kheda, Panchmahal, Dahod, Surendranagar, Rajkot, Amreli and other districts in the Saurashtra region, where very heavy rainfall is expected. Several other districts are likely to receive heavy rain with light thunderstorms.
For Saturday, IMD has placed Ahmedabad, Anand, Surendranagar and Rajkot under a red alert, indicating the possibility of another day of exceptionally heavy rainfall.
The latest system follows a series of intense rainfall events across Gujarat this monsoon. Valsad received 106 cm of rainfall on July 23, Vautha in Ahmedabad recorded 72 cm on July 24, and Santalpur in Patan logged 39 cm on July 25.
Flash flood alert for key districts
IMD issued a flash flood alert for Kheda, Anand, Panchmahal, Mahisagar, Dahod, Vadodara, Chhota Udepur, Narmada and Tapi districts in view of the prevailing atmospheric conditions. Surface runoff and inundation may occur in fully saturated soils and low-lying areas, IMD warned.
IMD listed several expected impacts of the inclement weather: breaking of tree branches and uprooting of trees; rain-induced damage to plantations, horticulture and standing crops; damage to vulnerable structures due to strong winds and rain; disruption to small ships, trawlers and boats; disruption of traffic movement; and localised landslides, mudslides, landslips, waterlogging, inundation and flooding in low-lying areas.
The weather office had also warned fishermen against venturing along and off the south Gujarat coast till August 3.
